title: Process Mapping & Improvement
description: Document current-state processes and design improvements. Tests BPMN notation, bottleneck analysis, and value stream mapping.

seo.overviewBody: Process mapping provides visual clarity on operational workflows, handoffs, and system interactions. Business analysts demonstrate value by creating BPMN 2.0 swimlane diagrams, modeling As-Is vs To-Be business processes, identifying operational bottlenecks, and quantifying cycle time improvements.

deliverables.title: 1. BPMN 2.0 Process Swimlane Diagram
deliverables.desc: Detailed BPMN 2.0 diagram mapping role swimlanes, start/end events, task activities, and decision gateways.

deliverables.title: 2. As-Is vs To-Be Process Optimization Spec
deliverables.desc: Comparative specification documenting baseline process friction points and streamlined To-Be target flows.

deliverables.title: 3. Operational Bottleneck Analysis Memo
deliverables.desc: Executive memo measuring task cycle times, queue delays, manual workarounds, and automation opportunities.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Exclusive (XOR) and Parallel (AND) gateways in BPMN 2.0?
faqs.answer: An Exclusive (XOR) gateway routes execution down exactly one path based on a condition. A Parallel (AND) gateway splits execution into multiple concurrent paths that run simultaneously.

faqs.question: Why are swimlanes essential in process modeling?
faqs.answer: Swimlanes visually segregate activities by department, role, or system, making organizational handoffs and accountability boundaries instantly clear.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an As-Is and To-Be process map?
faqs.answer: An As-Is map depicts current operational reality including inefficiencies. A To-Be map depicts the optimized future process state after proposed technical or procedural changes.
